newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares recover from Monday's plunge.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares recover from Monday's plunge.

text.p: The Hungarian share market regained some of Monday's sharp losses on Tuesday as investors found low prices to attractive to start new purchases, traders said.
The BUX index finished at 7,959.13 points, up 97.25 points or 1.24 percent.
"Monday's fall was very big...and many investors who missed the recent rally, might have decided to buy," said Andrea Keresztesi of ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett.
A stronger dollar and a rebound on Wall Street on Monday have also contributed to the rise, she added.
A strong dollar makes the forint, thus Hungarian shares cheaper for foreigners.
The Dow's moves are important because in central Europe the Budapest bourse it the most correlated to the Wall Street and due to the high proportion of foreign investors.
On Tuesday, pharmaceuticals Egis continued to fall in what traders attributed to its weak first half earnings released on Monday. Egis finished at 11,635 forints, down 665.
Elsewhere, the day's most actively traded oil firm MOL finished at 4,620 forints, up 160.
Among companies which released their first half results on Tuesday, mineral water bottler and distributor Kekkuti finished at 1,400 forints, down 50.
